correctness.rationale: For every n>=2 and 1<t<=2 the powered-distance quadratic reduces exactly to an analytically computed two-sector generalized eigenvalue pencil. Its upper symmetric root is strictly greater than n, the antisymmetric bound is strictly less than n, and the critical eigenvector is simple. The p interval, Schoenberg ranks and cubic asymptotic follow from explicit identities and a uniform perturbation bound. Independent finite numerical and exact-rational tests pass; universal proof is in RESULT.md.

value.rationale: An entire continuum of minimal local metric deformations is classified at its sharp Hilbert-snowflake threshold. The nontrivial cubic loss coefficient depends explicitly on edge weight, and strict multiplicity change proves a dimension jump. This is a natural metric stability problem and not a mere tabulation of an unweighted graph.
